Passed after Hamdan v. Rumsfeld struck down the commissions created by presidential order, it gave statutory authority to try alien unlawful enemy combatants by military commission and defined the offenses and procedures.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 109-366](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/109/public/366){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 10 U.S.C. 948a-950t](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/10/948a?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Added chapter 47A to Title 10: jurisdiction, procedures, and triable offenses for military commissions.
- Sec. 7: removed habeas jurisdiction over detained alien enemy combatants, held unconstitutional in Boumediene v. Bush (2008).
- Amended the War Crimes Act to narrow which Common Article 3 violations are federal crimes.
- 2009 revision: tighter rules on coerced statements and hearsay, and better access to counsel and evidence.

## Why it matters

It is the statutory basis for the Guantanamo commissions, whose jurisdiction depends on the armed conflict authorized by the [2001 AUMF](aumf-2001.qmd). It also amended the habeas provisions of the [Detainee Treatment Act](dta-2005.qmd).

## Current status

In force as replaced by the Military Commissions Act of 2009 (Title XVIII of the FY2010 National Defense Authorization Act, Pub. L. 111-84).

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}

## In the courts

- [Boumediene](../cases/boumediene-2008.qmd) (2008). Struck down Sec. 7, which barred habeas petitions from Guantanamo detainees.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [2001 AUMF](aumf-2001.qmd), [Detainee Treatment Act](dta-2005.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [NDAA (annual)](ndaa-annual.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 10 U.S.C.](title10-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** After September 11 ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 12: Civilian harm and the conduct of operations](../study/units/civilian-harm.qmd) (further reading).
